message.content:
**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference Guide to Its Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass | 1.00794 u (average) |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Diatomic molecule | H₂ |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive in air (range 4–75 % by volume) |
| | Reactivity with oxygen | Forms H₂O (combustion) |
| | Reactivity with halogens | Forms hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI) |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a weak acid in aqueous solution (pKa ≈ 3.2 for H₃O⁺) |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Strong H‑bond donor/acceptor in water and alcohols |
| | Solubility in water | 0.0006 g g⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; generally soluble in nonpolar solvents |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Most abundant; stable |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable; heavier; used in NMR, D₂O |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (β‑emitter); half‑life ≈ 12.32 y |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel cell technology | Hydrogen fuel cells (electrochemical conversion to electricity) |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Space propulsion | Liquid hydrogen as rocket propellant |
| | Medical imaging | Deuterium labeling in NMR spectroscopy |
| | Nuclear fusion research | Deuterium–tritium fusion in experimental reactors |
| | Food industry | Hydrogenation of oils, dehydrogenation of sugars |
| **Safety & Handling** | Explosion risk | Requires careful ventilation; use of inert atmosphere for handling |
| | Toxicity | Generally low; inhalation of high concentrations can cause asphyxiation |
| | Environmental impact | Low; hydrogen combustion produces only water vapor |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, and usually one neutron (protium).
- **It exists as a diatomic gas (H₂)** under normal conditions, but can form a variety of compounds (hydrides, acids, organics).
- **Its isotopes** (deuterium and tritium) have distinct physical and nuclear properties, making them useful in scientific research and industry.
- **Hydrogen’s reactivity** is high; it readily reacts with oxygen, halogens, and many metals, forming a wide range of products.
- **Applications** span from everyday uses (fuel cells, food processing) to cutting‑edge science (fusion energy, medical imaging).

Feel free to ask if you’d like more detail on any specific property or application!
